title: The Birth of John the Baptist (24 June)
hookLine: with Jesus and Mary, one of only three births in the calendar

cards: Saints are almost always remembered on the day they died: the day of death is the birthday into heaven. But three people get a feast for the day they were born. Jesus, on Christmas.

Mary, in September. And one more, today, the twenty-fourth of June, six months before Christmas, near the longest day of the year in the north. In parts of Europe people still light bonfires on the night before.
The baby is John, who'd grow up to baptize in the Jordan, and his birth starts with a man who can't speak.

teach.b: Luke tells it. Zachary is an old priest, and his wife Elizabeth has never had children. While he's serving in the Temple, an angel tells him they'll have a son, and Zachary doubts it.
So he's struck mute until the day it comes true. Months of silence. The baby is born, and on the eighth day the relatives gather for the circumcision and the naming.
Everyone assumes he'll be called Zachary, after his father. Elizabeth says no, he'll be called John.

teach.h: NOBODY IN YOUR FAMILY HAS THAT NAME.
teach.b: They argue: nobody in your family has that name. So they turn to the father and make signs at him. And Zachary, in the Douay-Rheims, "demanding a writing table, he wrote, saying: John is his name."
Instantly his tongue is loosed, and he starts praising God. The song he sings, the Benedictus, is the Gospel canticle of Morning Prayer in the Liturgy of the Hours.
The name John comes from the Hebrew Yohanan, God has been gracious. Choosing it meant breaking with family custom to follow what had been given. And why late June?
Luke says Elizabeth was six months along when the angel came to Mary, so the calendar puts John six months before Christmas.

teach.h: THE DAYS SHORTEN AFTER HIS BIRTH.
teach.b: Saint Augustine noticed that after John's birth the days start to shorten, and after Christ's they start to lengthen.

teach.h: HE MUST INCREASE: BUT I MUST DECREASE.
teach.b: He heard in it John's own line, from the fourth Gospel: "He must increase: but I must decrease." A whole life pointing past itself, built into the sunlight.

how: Catholics celebrate the Nativity of John the Baptist as a solemnity on 24 June; in parts of Europe and Latin America, Saint John's Eve is kept with bonfires and festivals, and clergy and religious pray his father's song, the Benedictus, every morning.

games.q: you're Zachary, still unable to speak. the relatives are arguing over your son's name and turn to you. what do you do?
o: nod along with naming him Zachary.
ask for a writing tablet and write: John is his name.
leave the decision to the elders.
games.why: he writes, John is his name, and at once his tongue is loosed and he praises God.

practice: Bring to mind, one at a time, the family you were born into: parents, brothers and sisters, grandparents, whoever was there at the start.
For some that's warm, for some it's complicated, painful or unknown, and that's all right; just hold what's true.
If you pray, you can pray for each of them by name; if you don't, wish each one peace, including anyone you've lost touch with.

wordCard.voice: Yohanan. The Hebrew name, God has been gracious, that Zachary wrote on the tablet when his tongue was freed. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: Yohanan, God has been gracious — the name Zachary wrote on the tablet.

carryVoice: Your line: his name is john. A father's tongue, loosed by writing a name. Until tomorrow.
